dialect.detail: Likely RM-COBOL or ACU-style dialect given DISPLAY ... LINE ... POSITION ... ERASE screen handling syntax, common in PC/microcomputer COBOL environments (e.g. RM-COBOL, Micro Focus, or similar Latin American educational tools)
evidence: ASSIGN TO DISK INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM

purpose.domain_detail: Student exercise for indexed file deletion; manages a customer (CLIENTES) indexed file with fields for client ID, name, card ID, card type, annual fee, and registration date
purpose.summary: This program opens an indexed customer file and allows the user to search for a customer by ID, display the record, and optionally delete it. It loops until the user chooses to stop. It is a simple interactive batch program demonstrating indexed file DELETE operations.

notable_features: Indexed file with RANDOM access mode and RECORD KEY
Screen-oriented DISPLAY/ACCEPT with LINE and POSITION clauses and ERASE
No COPY statements, no CALL statements, no COMP-3 usage
verdict.notes: Comment at top in Spanish: 'MI PROGRAMA DE ELIMINAR REGISTROS DE ARCHIVOS INDEXADOS' (my program to delete records from indexed files). The LINE/POSITION/ERASE syntax in DISPLAY/ACCEPT is characteristic of RM-COBOL or similar PC COBOL dialects common in Latin American academic settings. Minor typo in source: 'ELIMIAR' instead of 'ELIMINAR'. File decoded with latin-1 due to accented characters (¿, é).
